pages.title: Claim an early years teacher recognition payment

components.text: Use this service to claim a recognition payment if you're an eligible early years teacher.
You must meet the eligibility criteria for the early years teacher recognition payment. Read the [guidance](https://example.com) for full details about who can claim and how the payment works.
What you need
You will need:

your Teacher Reference Number (TRN) - you'll have one if you have, or are working towards, Early Years Professional Status (EYPS), qualified teacher status (QTS) or early years teacher status (EYTS)

a GOV.UK One Login account to prove your identity - you'll need a UK passport, UK photo driving licence or biometric residence permit to set it up

your bank details, including the full name on the account, sort code and account number

your gender as it appears on payroll

a recent payslip from the last 2 months
Before you start
If you need to [find a lost TRN](find-a-lost-trn), do this before you claim. It can take 5 working days to recover your TRN.
If you need to set up a GOV.UK One Login account, this can take 2 weeks.
How long it takes to claim
If you have your TRN and One Login account it takes around 10 minutes to submit a claim.
Continue

pages.title: You are not eligible for this payment

components.text:
To be eligible for the early years teacher recognition payment you must be a qualified early years teacher in an eligible local authority area.

If you think this is a mistake, check your answers or contact us at EYTrecognitionpayment@education.gov.uk

pages.title: Sign in with GOV.UK One Login

components.text: You will need to sign in to your GOV.UK One Login account to apply. If you don't have an account yet, we will help you create one.
To create a GOV.UK One Login account, you will need:

an email address
a way to get security codes - this can be a mobile phone number or an authenticator app
When you have signed in to GOV.UK One Login, you will return to this service to complete your application.
You must prove your identity using the GOV.UK One Login service to submit a claim for a recognition payment.
Continue

pages.title: Continue to the service you need to use

components.text: You've successfully proved your identity. You can now continue to the service you need to use.
Some of the information you shared when you proved your identity might be used to automatically fill in forms within the service.
Continue

pages.title: You may be eligible for a recognition payment of up to £4,500

components.text: We've confirmed your identity and that you have an eligible qualification. We still need to review your employment evidence before we can make a decision.
Before you continue your claim

The payment may affect your finances. You should check how it could impact you before you decide whether to accept it. While the payment is £4,500, the amount paid into your account may be lower if you need to pay tax or repay your student loan.
Student loan deductions

If you pay [the basic rate of Income Tax](https://www.gov.uk/income-tax-rates#income-tax-rates-and-bands), we will pay tax and National Insurance for you and you will receive the full amount. You may have to pay additional Income Tax if you pay the higher rate.
Benefits
The payment may affect any benefits you receive. You should [check how they might be affected](https://www.gov.uk/benefits-calculators) before you accept the payment.

components.hint: If you click no, you'll cancel your claim and exit the service.

components.text: Student loan deductions
We'll check if you're repaying a student loan. If you are, we'll take the right amount from your recognition payment automatically.
Income Tax
We'll check if you pay the higher rate of Income Tax. If you do, we'll take any extra tax you owe from your payment. You do not need to do anything.
To pay you
The Department of Education (DfE) will make the payment directly to you. To complete the rest of your application, you'll need your:

home address
gender as it appears in payroll
bank account details
